name: Tropical rainforest
notes: Ever-wet lowland rainforest: multi-layered evergreen broadleaf forest with buttressed canopy, giant emergents, palms, lianas and heavy epiphyte load. Drawn on the Amazon, Congo Basin and Sundaland (Borneo/Malaya) dipterocarp forest.

emergent.silhouette: tall straight bole with small round crown above canopy

growth.juvenile_note: The big woody seed germinates slowly: often 12-18 months after an agouti buries it (1-3 months if the shell is removed). A shoot with small scale leaves comes first, then true leaves. The sapling is a straight, slender whip with large, leathery, oblong, wavy-edged leaves; in shade it can wait for years almost dormant, then rockets up when a treefall opens a gap.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 50 m, lives 500 to ~1000 yr, saplings wait years in shade for a gap); Brazil-nut agronomy and extractive-reserve studies (intact seeds germinate after 12-18 months, 1-3 months without testa; plantation seedlings fruit from ~10-15 yr, grafts ~8 yr); height-growth timings estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (cream 6-petalled flowers with a hood-shaped stamen mass, one-day flowers pollinated only by large bees: Bombus, Centris, Epicharis, Eulaema, Xylocopa; capsule 10-15 cm, up to 2 kg, 8-24 seeds, 14 months from pollination to ripe; agoutis open fallen fruit); fruit set and crop from harvest studies, approximate.

The sapling has a smooth GREEN trunk studded with stout conical thorns and grows straight and fast, with horizontal branches in widely spaced whorls, giving a tiered pagoda-like cone before it later spreads into a flat emergent crown on huge buttresses.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Ceiba pentandra (white to rose petals, flowers open soon after dark, fruit bats, hawkmoths and bees; capsule 10-30 cm, 120-175 seeds); Wikipedia (to 60 m, 5-9 leaflets, several hundred pods per tree); growth, first flowering and lifespan estimated from PROSEA-style kapok data

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Ceiba pentandra (flowers in dry season on leafless branches, open at dusk for one night, bats then moths and bees; capsules 10-30 cm split along 5 lines releasing kapok floss and 120-175 seeds); Wikipedia (several hundred pods per tree)

Saplings are slim whips with smooth pale bark that race upward in gaps; the huge plank buttresses and the smooth, pale grey-white bole of the emergent giant come only after decades, once the crown breaks through the canopy.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Koompassia excelsa: to 85-88 m, among the tallest tropical trees; giant honey bees hang combs from its branches); growth, age and germination estimated from Koompassia and other light-demanding Malesian emergents.

fruiting.source: Estimated from genus Koompassia: tiny whitish flowers in large terminal panicles during supra-annual general-flowering years, thin flat papery one-seeded wind-dispersed pods; no species-specific phenology data found.

Seedlings wait for decades as a seedling bank in deep forest shade, then shoot up as slender whips in a gap; the tree later becomes a huge emergent with a buttressed pale trunk and a broad cauliflower crown.
growth.source: Wikipedia Shorea (Richetia) faguetiana (tallest tropical tree, 'Menara' in Danum Valley ~98-100 m; Borneo, Malay Peninsula, Thailand); PROSEA 5(1) dipterocarps (recalcitrant seed germinating in days, supra-annual mast flowering, yellow meranti relatively shade tolerant, slow); growth curve, first seed and lifespan estimated

fruiting.source: PROSEA and Appanah/Ashton on Shorea: flowers only in general (mast) flowering years every 2-10 yr, small cream flowers open one night in big panicles, pollinated by thrips and small beetles (thrips not a listed guild); nut with 3 long and 2 short wings ripens ~3-4 months later and spins down; very low fruit set; crop estimated

The sapling is a fast single leader that throws out tiers of horizontal branches in whorls, giving a pagoda-like look; later a tall, straight bole with thin plank buttresses and a flat, spreading crown, bare in the dry season.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (Terminalia superba: to 50 m, buttresses to 6 m; sexual maturity at ~15 yr in Cote d'Ivoire, 23 yr in Congo, 6-10 yr in plantations; rotation ~40 yr; stored seed 40-60% germination); Wikipedia (to 60 m, deciduous Nov-Feb). Ripening and crop estimated.

canopy.name: Moriche palm

growth.juvenile_note: The seed sends a germination tube down into the wet soil from which the seedling rises. The first leaves are simple, strap-like pleated blades; later leaves turn into huge rounded costapalmate fans on long stalks. For years it is a stemless tuft of fans in the swamp while the trunk base thickens underground, then a smooth grey column rises and old leaves fall cleanly away.
growth.source: Wikipedia Mauritia flexuosa (to 35 m, flowers Dec-Apr, scaly chestnut fruit with yellow pulp, seeds float and are spread by floods and fish); palm establishment and growth rates estimated from Mauritia/Neotropical fan-palm literature

canopy.source: Palm of Amazon and Orinoco swamps; height 20-35 m. Fan palm of the swamps; buriti. Standard floras and Kew POWO for the name.

growth.juvenile_note: The seedling is a grassy tuft of thin leafy shoots. Each rainy season the young clump sends up stouter culms than the year before, reaching full-size culms (up to ~30 m tall, 20-28 cm thick) after roughly a decade. New shoots are fat conical spears wrapped in large brown hairy sheaths that elongate up to 40 cm a day; culm branches and leaves appear only after the culm reaches full height.
growth.source: Wikipedia Dendrocalamus giganteus (to 30 m, record 42 m; culms to 28 cm thick; up to 40 cm/day, record 46 cm in 24 h at Peradeniya; dense clumps). shrub.name: Giant taro

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: one small heart- to arrow-shaped leaf on a thin stalk from a pea-sized corm, then a low rosette of a few glossy green arrowhead leaves on long fleshy stalks. Within 1-2 years a thick, ringed, above-ground stem forms and suckers sprout at its base; leaves grow to 1-2 m, held nearly upright with the tip pointing up.
growth.source: Useful Tropical Plants (Alocasia macrorrhizos: 2-4 m, occasionally 5; stems to 3 m or more and 20 cm thick; 400-600 days to mature; seed germinates best at 24 C; grows best in some shade, tolerates full sun and deep shade; thermogenic spadix, insect-pollinated). Germination days, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings in mud or shallow water first make a small rosette of narrow, strap- to lance-shaped submerged leaves; as the plant grows it switches to big, erect emergent leaves: ovate, heart-based blades 15-26 cm long on stalks up to 80-120 cm, with prominent arching veins. ground.name: Common swamp pitcher

growth.source: Estimated from lowland Nepenthes: Wikipedia N. mirabilis (the most widespread pitcher plant, in open swampy and disturbed lowland sites, stems to several m, dimorphic pitchers); growers' data for germination and first flowering

ground.name: Taro

growth.juvenile_note: Almost always grows from a corm or side cormel (true seed is rare): a pointed shoot unrolls into a small rosette of long-stalked leaves. Blades are heart- to arrow-shaped and peltate (stalk joined inside the blade), velvety and water-repellent; each new leaf is bigger until the clump of 'elephant ear' leaves on 1 m stalks is reached in 5-7 months, with cormels budding around the base.
growth.source: Wikipedia Taro (leaves to 40 x 25 cm on 0.8-1.2 m petioles; matures 6-12 months after planting on dry land, 12-15 months in wetland, early cultivars 5-7 months; propagated by corms and cormels; perennial); PROSEA/FAO taro accounts (sprouting in 2-4 weeks, flowering rare, grows in partial shade)

repro.note: giant herbs, not trees: each stem grows in a season, fruits or flowers once and dies, replaced by suckers from the clump — fast growth stages, visible in weeks

ground.source: SE Asia; wet fields and stream banks everywhere in the tropics. The staple root of the wet tropics; camp folk plant it in water; camp-follower. Kew POWO.

epiphyte.name: Golden pothos

growth.juvenile_note: No seed is known: plants spread from stem pieces, which root at a node in 1-2 weeks and push a new shoot in 2-4 weeks (the values given). Juvenile shoots creep over the ground and up trunks with small (under 20 cm) entire, heart-shaped glossy leaves, green marbled yellow. High on a tree the leaves swell to 60-100 cm and become irregularly pinnatifid or holed.
growth.source: Wikipedia (juvenile leaves <20 cm, adult to 100 x 45 cm pinnatifid; climbs to 20 m; endemic to Mo'orea); Hung et al. 2016 Scientific Reports (GA-deficient, no flowering recorded since 1962; adult leaves several-fold larger); UW-Madison Extension (pothos). Climbing rate and ages estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds sprout with two thick, rounded cotyledons, then the typical two-lobed 'cow-hoof' leaves. The seedling is a self-supporting whip that soon becomes a searching shoot with paired coiled tendrils. Young stems are round; only older climbing stems flatten and fold into the wavy, ribbon-like 'monkey ladder' that hangs from the canopy.

fruiting.source: Estimated from Schnella/Bauhinia lianas: small white 5-petalled flowers in dense racemes on canopy branch tips, visited by bees and butterflies; flat woody pods that twist open explosively; timings and counts estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings creep across the dark forest floor away from the light (skototropism) until they touch a tree trunk, then climb it. Juvenile leaves are small, entire and heart-shaped, often pressed flat against the bark like shingles; higher up the leaves get huge, deeply split and holed (fenestrated) on long stalks, and cord-like aerial roots dangle to the ground.
growth.source: Wikipedia Monstera deliciosa (seedlings grow towards darkness until they find a trunk; juvenile leaves entire, later lobed and fenestrate; climbs to 20 m; flowers ~3 yr after planting in ideal conditions); vine lifespan estimated
